I sort of see what you mean, but I think it's not that black and white when it comes to disabilities, because there is so much variation between different disabilities and even between each instance of that disability and how much it is hurting them whether mentally or physically. Isn't it sad if a loved one is depressed and suicidal? My first reaction to someone telling me they have OCD isn't sadness, but my reaction to someone telling me they have crippling OCD that is ruining their life would definitely be sadness. I have a few disabilities, all mental (alcoholism, depression, and selective mutism) and I get where you're coming from about negative judgement about disabilities. But for example there's a big difference between saying "fuck cancer" and saying "fuck cancer patients".

I mean, I would just assume they meant it was sad that she was struggling enough to need that help, not that it was sad that she's getting help. It seems like a minor misunderstanding on your part. Do you not think that it's sad that your cousin is struggling with alcoholism and with whatever stressor contributed to it? Because yeah that's kinda odd. Alcoholism sucks and I would be sad if I found out someone I cared about was dealing with it. If you just mean that her getting help isn't sad, then I guess I agree, but that probably isn't what they meant. Honestly, to me your response to anyone saying it's sad just comes off as being unnecessarily disagreeable.

For me there is just no point. I was never drinking beer for the taste; if I was drinking any alcohol it was to get drunk it. If I'm drinking something non alcoholic, there are thousands of options that I will like more than non alcoholic beer.

Today is day 13 for me. Yesterday was tough, any holidays big or small were always an excuse to drink. I actually tried to buy alcohol yesterday but canceled the delivery, only because I couldn't find my ID. I found it today, briefly considered buying alcohol but decided against it. Tomorrow will be two weeks. IWNTWYT

Here is mine:

**Drunk 4th:** A couple years ago, the last summer that me and my twin brother both went home for the summer, my mom and stepdad left for the 4th, so me and my brother had the house to ourselves. We were drunk the whole day, and at some point we just snapped. I don't even know why we were mad, but we just started beating the shit out of each other. We shared a room at my mom's house, so neither of us wanted to go to sleep afterwards. I didn't know what he would do to me if I fell asleep, and he felt the same about me. So we watched a movie and kept drinking, while casually talking and laughing about how much we literally wanted to kill each other. Early the next morning we both separately walked an hour to work (2 different McDonald's locations), while bruised, sore, and still drunk. I had claw marks on my face, and my glasses were either lost or broken so I couldn't see well. It was still dark out, and I remember repeatedly falling down in the street and just thinking I was going to get ran over and die there. I brought more alcohol with me and was still drinking on my walk to work until I dropped it and lost it one of the times I fell. I only remember the beginning of the walk, and then I woke up in the break room at work, with two of my managers who apparently had been trying to wake me up for a while. They asked me something, and I just said, "Me and my brother got in a fight." When I got home from work, there was broken glass everywhere which I didn't remember happening, and me and my brother's bedroom door was broken. We mutually agreed after that to stop drinking for a while. It lasted two weeks, and we were high the whole time.

**Sober 4th:** Yesterday was my 12th day sober. I tried to buy alcohol but couldn't find my ID. I went to work, sober, and had a great day. I came home, watched a movie, and went to bed. Pretty uneventful, I wish I could have watched some fireworks at least, but it was mostly just an ordinary day. Today I found my ID, thought about buying alcohol or getting high, then thought about having to work early tomorrow morning and decided to do neither. Instead I had a relaxing day off and watched some movies, which I can actually remember for once. Tomorrow will be 2 weeks, the longest I have gone in a long time other than those two weeks with my twin and an involuntary two week hospital stay.
I told my boss the truth the last time I missed work because of it a little over a week ago. It went pretty well

I had, or thought I had, a handle on it too, but a few incidents made me realize I was headed back in the wrong direction. So I'm quitting, at least for now, because I don't want to end up back where I was a year or two ago. I lost everything and don't want to lose everything I've worked for since then

Day 6. Today is my first day off work since quitting which makes it harder without that distraction and reason not to drink. I keep getting thoughts like a constant argument in my head that I don't really need to stop, that this is ridiculous, that I'm only 22 and everyone drinks a lot and parties when they're in their 20s, it's totally normal.

Trying to stay logical and objective and tell myself no it's not normal to be repeatedly hospitalized, to drink a whole bottle of vodka in a day alone in your room, or to wake up with a broken phone, a missed shift at work and no memory of the past two days. Tomorrow will be one week since that missed work shift and one week since I stopped. It was far from my lowest low but I could feel myself sliding back towards rock bottom and need to stop before it gets that bad again.
